acceptance: T1 Positive recovery: actual MCP/service recovery into a second clean worktree and an independent URL-matching clone succeeds after the original checkout path is unavailable; subsequent readiness/prepare/advance/final validation use the new path; prepared receipts remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

T2 Negative recovery: wrong owner/generation/epoch/path/head, incomplete relocation tuple, dirty destination, wrong branch/repository, missing history and stale CAS all refuse without publishing any partial ownership/path change. A simulated retry-time destination mutation is revalidated. Completed/aborted batches and prohibited late moves retain their existing refusals.

T3 Idempotency and history: exact retry creates no extra transition; retry with the same new generation but a different relocation tuple or reason refuses. Old owner writes fail after recovery; accepted-member ancestry, scope, final-PR identity and partial-closeout restrictions remain. Historical member paths/epochs are not rewritten and copied old-location final evidence cannot pass.

T4 Capability: initialize and batch-show expose the same additive relocation feature from the installed runtime; absent feature is distinguishable from support. Legacy same-path owner recovery remains usable. No store or receipt migration occurs on ordinary operations or upgrade.

T5 CLI freshness: an actual show command reads a field larger than its budget through all --rev continuations; the concatenated content is exact. Moved revision refuses/restarts rather than mixing pages; offline/cache output remains explicitly stale without authoritative rev.

T6 Regression rubric: failing-before/passing-after tests cover the consumer-visible recovery and pagination boundaries; existing schema-4, claims, prepare/advance/rebind/finish and extra-member acceptance behaviors still pass. Run actual stdio MCP/CLI smoke from a clean installed candidate outside the source tree; tests alone are not the smoke proof.

T7 Documentation and delivery: ADR 0012, public API/CLI/capability and release notes describe the narrow immutability exception and trust limit. Skill-sync pins the prerequisite catalog revision. One scoped PR merges through required gates; the GitHub release is based on the merged revision and its wheel/sdist/SHA256SUMS exist.

T8 Released-byte proof: install the exact released wheel in an isolated environment, verify it against release checksums, run initialize and read-only/scratch-store recovery/CLI smoke without sibling-source imports, and record tag/source revision/asset hashes/results. Do not activate BenchBox or wait for its downstream item here.

description:
Objective: deliver the smallest generic runtime changes needed by the simplified batch workflow, as one joeharris76/todo-db PR followed by its GitHub release. This task does NOT wait for BenchBox consumer activation; that belongs to batch-remediation-benchbox-20261102, avoiding a circular dependency.

Prior art: extend src/todo_db/service.py recover_batch_owner and source-checkout validation, src/todo_db/store.py owner recovery/CAS/audit, existing MCP exposure/capability and src/todo_db/cli.py section reads. Preserve ADR 0012 caller-attested evidence and advisory identity, prepared_work_v2 receipts, schema-4 stores, owner-only claims, acceptance_required and current-acceptance validation. Existing extra-member acceptance already supports BenchBox's all-member final reruns; do not replace it with a new evidence framework.

Implementation: add an optional all-or-nothing recovery tuple expected_integration_worktree, expected_integration_head, integration_worktree. Preserve same-path owner-only recovery. For relocation CAS old owner/generation/path/head and require new generation/session attribution; re-prove the clean canonical destination, registered branch/repository, exact expected head and recorded/member ancestry on EVERY mutation retry. Atomically rotate owner and current checkout path, increment epoch and audit old/new path and expected head. Bind idempotent retries to the full request; wrong destination/reason/expectations must not silently succeed. Keep receipts and historical source paths unchanged. Scope, branch, repository, start/accepted heads, final PR and log identity cannot be edited through relocation. Existing local-path repository identity restrictions remain; independent URL-matching clones are the BenchBox use case.

Advertise todo_db_batch.features.integration_worktree_relocation=true in initialize and matching read-only capability output. Clients without it must refuse relocation, not fall back. Keep store/receipt schema versions unless demonstrated incompatibility forces a genuinely new owner decision; no speculative schema cutover. Fix todo-db show CLI continuation to accept/pass --rev, including requested pages at one revision. Preserve existing stale envelopes; stale reads never acquire authoritative rev by relabelling cached_rev.

Delivery gates: consume the exact catalog revision from the prerequisite using supported skill-sync. Re-read release/version conventions; choose the next repository-appropriate version, merge the reviewed PR, publish its supported GitHub tag/wheel/sdist/checksums through the normal workflow, then smoke the exact released wheel in isolation. A source checkout or locally built candidate is not proof of the released artifact. Export release/tag/source/full asset hashes and capability proof to the BenchBox task. BenchBox vendoring/relock and affected local MCP activation happen in that downstream task, not as a prerequisite to finishing this one.

Guardrails: no mutable-repository or unguarded path reassignment API; no rewriting prepared/finished-member provenance; no real BenchBox tracker cutover/repair in runtime regression fixtures; no new registry/index API merely for markerless discovery; no source-version hardcoding in incidental tests. Authorize GitHub release/assets only, not PyPI/cloud publication or unrelated process restarts.
